title: Amazing Animals
intro: From octopuses to pandas, test what you know about the wonderful creatures of our planet.

questions.prompt: How many arms does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: An octopus has eight arms covered in suckers, which it uses to grab, taste and move.

questions.prompt: A blue whale is a mammal, not a fish.
questions.explanation: Whales are mammals. They breathe air through blowholes and feed their babies milk.

questions.prompt: What do giraffes mostly eat?
questions.explanation: Giraffes use their long necks and tongues to reach leaves high up in trees.

questions.prompt: Where do emperor penguins live in the wild?
questions.explanation: Emperor penguins live in and around Antarctica, one of the coldest places on Earth.

questions.prompt: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.explanation: Baby kangaroos are called joeys. They grow inside their mother's pouch.

questions.prompt: What do giant pandas mostly eat?
questions.explanation: Bamboo makes up almost all of a giant panda's diet, and they eat a lot of it every day.

questions.prompt: Polar bears have black skin under their fur.
questions.explanation: A polar bear's fur looks white, but the skin underneath is black, which helps soak up warmth from the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which of these animals is a reptile?
questions.explanation: Komodo dragons are lizards, and lizards are reptiles with dry, scaly skin.

questions.prompt: What is the long, bendy nose of an elephant called?
questions.explanation: An elephant's trunk is its nose and upper lip joined together. It uses it to breathe, smell, drink and pick things up.

questions.prompt: What is a group of lions called?
questions.explanation: Lions live together in groups called prides, usually made up of related females, their cubs and a few males.

questions.prompt: In a honeybee hive, which bee lays all the eggs?
questions.explanation: Each hive has one queen bee. Her job is to lay the eggs that become the next generation of bees.

questions.prompt: What do honeybees make from the nectar they collect from flowers?
questions.explanation: Honeybees carry nectar back to the hive and turn it into honey, which feeds the colony through the winter.

questions.prompt: How does a honeybee tell the others in its hive where to find good flowers?
questions.explanation: A honeybee does a waggle dance in a figure-of-eight shape. The way it waggles shows the other bees which way to fly for food.

questions.prompt: What is a group of zebras called?
questions.explanation: Zebras live and travel together in herds. Staying together helps them spot danger on the African grasslands.

questions.prompt: What does a hedgehog do to protect itself when it feels in danger?

options.label: It rolls into a spiky ball

questions.explanation: A hedgehog tucks in its head and legs and curls into a tight ball, so only its prickly spines are showing.

questions.prompt: Brown bears spend the coldest part of winter in a long, deep sleep in their dens. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Hibernation is a deep winter rest. Brown bears eat lots in autumn to build up fat, then live off it while they sleep.

questions.prompt: Brown bears eat berries, roots and fish. What do we call an animal that eats both plants and meat?
questions.explanation: An omnivore eats both plants and animals. Brown bears will happily munch on berries one day and catch salmon the next.

questions.prompt: Where do flamingos get their pink colour from?
questions.explanation: Flamingos eat tiny shrimps and algae that contain pink colouring. Without that food, their feathers slowly turn pale.

questions.prompt: Ladybirds belong to which group of insects?
questions.explanation: Ladybirds are small beetles. They are also known as lady beetles or ladybird beetles.

questions.prompt: Which of these animals is famous for changing the colour of its skin?
questions.explanation: Chameleons change colour to show their mood, warm up or cool down, and send messages to other chameleons.

questions.prompt: Clownfish make their homes among the stinging tentacles of which sea creature?
questions.explanation: Clownfish are covered in a special slime that protects them, so they can hide safely among a sea anemone's stinging tentacles.

questions.prompt: Snowy owls mainly live in which cold part of the world?
questions.explanation: Snowy owls live mainly in the Arctic, on open treeless land called tundra. Their white feathers help them blend in with the snow.

questions.prompt: North American monarch butterflies are famous for doing what every autumn?

options.label: Flying huge distances to warmer places

questions.explanation: Every autumn, millions of monarch butterflies make a long migration south to escape the cold, travelling thousands of kilometres.

questions.prompt: Gardeners like ladybirds because they eat which tiny plant pests?
questions.explanation: Ladybirds gobble up aphids, tiny insects that suck the juice out of plants. One ladybird can eat thousands in its lifetime.

questions.prompt: No two zebras have exactly the same pattern of stripes.
questions.explanation: Every zebra's stripes are unique, a bit like your fingerprints.

questions.prompt: Clownfish are a kind of fish that live on coral reefs.
questions.explanation: Clownfish live in warm, shallow coral reefs in the Pacific and Indian oceans, sheltering among sea anemones.

questions.prompt: If a sea star loses an arm, it can grow a new one.
questions.explanation: Sea stars, also called starfish, can regrow lost arms. It takes a long time, but the new arm grows back.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: An octopus has three hearts. Two pump blood through its gills and the third pumps blood around the rest of its body.

questions.prompt: Most sea stars have how many arms?
questions.explanation: Most sea stars have five arms, although some kinds can have many more.

questions.prompt: Galápagos giant tortoises can live to be over how many years old?
questions.explanation: Galápagos tortoises are among the longest-living animals, and many live to be over 100 years old.
